title: Are You Consistent But Still Struggling?
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Writing amid pandemic-era classroom strain, Linsin argues that consistent consequences alone are not enough — what makes consequences matter is whether students genuinely enjoy being in the classroom. He claims that negativity in schools has caused teachers to lose sight of this experiential quality, and that restoring it now takes less effort than it did before the pandemic. He offers a list of small, low-cost teacher behaviors — smiling, joking, laughing, emoting, demanding high standards, inviting participation, enthusing, reading aloud, keeping the class moving, staying positive, and refusing to settle for less — as levers that can visibly change a class within days. The piece closes with a call to personal responsibility, urging teachers to close their classroom door on outside negativity and take ownership of the tone and experience they create, for their students' sake and their own.
points: Consistent consequences only work when paired with a classroom experience students genuinely enjoy being part of.
Pandemic-era negativity eroded the enjoyable classroom experience that makes accountability meaningful.
Small, low-effort teacher behaviors — smiling, joking, emoting, reading aloud, keeping momentum — can visibly shift a class within days.
Teachers can raise both behavioral and academic expectations even amid outside difficulty; students respond to purpose and discipline.
Teachers can close their classroom door on outside negativity and take full ownership of the tone and culture inside it.
quotes: It’s to create a learning experience your students love being part of. This is the secret . It always has been and always will be.

The good news is that it doesn’t take much. In fact, it takes less than before the pandemic. Small changes, reminders of old, that if you begin using on Monday, you’ll have a different class by Friday.
Boldly raise standards on behavior and academic expectations. Your students are yearning for purpose and discipline and will thrive because of it.
Accept nothing less than the classroom you want and know is best for your students, Covid be damned, and that’s what you’ll get.
Only you can brighten and improve their learning experience. So take responsibility. Fix the tone and tenor of your classroom.
It really doesn’t take a lot. A tweak here and there, a turn in attitude, an embrace of what is good and right and a dose of determination.
